definition: A ceremony at which degrees or diplomas are conferred; a graduation ceremony
contextSentence: Steve Jobs delivered a commencement address at Stanford University.
contextSentenceKo: 스티브 잡스는 스탠퍼드 대학교에서 졸업 축사를 했습니다.

definition: The act of legally taking another's child and raising it as one's own
etymology: From Latin 'adoptio', from 'adoptare' (to choose for oneself)
contextSentence: She decided to put me up for adoption.
contextSentenceKo: 그녀는 저를 입양 보내기로 결심했습니다.

definition: Not married
contextSentence: My biological mother was a young, unwed graduate student.
contextSentenceKo: 제 생모는 젊은 미혼 대학원생이었습니다.

definition: To become less severe or intense; to finally agree after initially refusing
contextSentence: She only relented a few months later when my parents promised that I would go to college.
contextSentenceKo: 부모님이 제가 대학에 가겠다고 약속한 후에야 몇 달 뒤에 그녀는 마음을 바꿨습니다.

definition: In a way that shows a lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment
contextSentence: But I naively chose a college that was almost as expensive as Stanford.
contextSentenceKo: 하지만 저는 순진하게도 스탠퍼드만큼이나 비싼 대학을 선택했습니다.

definition: The art of producing decorative handwriting or lettering with a pen or brush
contextSentence: Reed College at that time offered perhaps the best calligraphy instruction in the country.
contextSentenceKo: 당시 리드 칼리지는 아마도 미국에서 최고의 서예 수업을 제공했습니다.

definition: A small line or stroke attached to the end of a larger stroke in a letter or symbol in certain typefaces
contextSentence: I learned about serif and sans-serif typefaces.
contextSentenceKo: 저는 세리프체와 산세리프체에 대해 배웠습니다.

definition: The art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible, readable, and appealing
contextSentence: It was beautiful, historical, artistically subtle in a way that science can't capture.
contextSentenceKo: 그것은 과학으로는 포착할 수 없는 방식으로 아름답고, 역사적이며, 예술적으로 섬세했습니다.

definition: The ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning
contextSentence: Curiosity and intuition turned out to be priceless later on.
contextSentenceKo: 호기심과 직관은 나중에 값을 매길 수 없을 만큼 소중한 것으로 밝혀졌습니다.

definition: To separate from another route or path; to differ or deviate in opinion or direction
contextSentence: But then our visions of the future began to diverge.
contextSentenceKo: 하지만 미래에 대한 우리의 비전이 서로 갈라지기 시작했습니다.

definition: Highly destructive or damaging; causing severe shock, distress, or grief
contextSentence: What had been the focus of my entire adult life was gone. And it was devastating.
contextSentenceKo: 제 성인 생활 전체의 초점이었던 것이 사라졌습니다. 정말 충격적이었습니다.

definition: A person who organizes and operates a business, taking on greater than normal financial risks
contextSentence: I felt that I had let the previous generation of entrepreneurs down.
contextSentenceKo: 저는 이전 세대의 기업가들을 실망시켰다고 느꼈습니다.

definition: A revival of or renewed interest in something; a period of new growth or activity
etymology: From French 'renaissance' (rebirth), from Latin 're-' (again) + 'nasci' (to be born)
contextSentence: The technology we developed at Next is at the heart of Apple's current renaissance.
contextSentenceKo: 넥스트에서 개발한 기술이 애플의 현재 부흥의 핵심에 있습니다.

definition: A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true
etymology: From Greek 'dogma' (opinion, belief), from 'dokein' (to seem good)
contextSentence: Don't be trapped by dogma, which is living with the results of other people's thinking.
contextSentenceKo: 도그마에 갇히지 마세요. 그것은 다른 사람들의 생각의 결과에 따라 사는 것입니다.

definition: In a way that corresponds in size or amount to something else; in proper proportion
contextSentence: The Mac would have never had multiple typefaces or proportionally spaced fonts.
contextSentenceKo: 맥은 다양한 서체나 비례 간격 폰트를 갖추지 못했을 것입니다.

definition: A stick or staff passed from runner to runner in a relay race; figuratively, a responsibility passed on
contextSentence: That I had dropped the baton as it was being passed to me.
contextSentenceKo: 바통이 제게 전달되는 과정에서 제가 그것을 놓쳐버렸다고요.

definition: To trip or momentarily lose one's balance; to come across or find something by chance
etymology: From Middle English 'stumblen', related to Old Norse 'stumra'
contextSentence: Much of what I stumbled into by following my curiosity turned out to be priceless.
contextSentenceKo: 호기심을 따라가다가 우연히 마주친 것들의 대부분이 나중에 매우 귀중한 것으로 밝혀졌습니다.

definition: So precious that its value cannot be determined; invaluable
meaningKo: 값을 매길 수 없는, 매우 귀중한
contextSentence: Curiosity and intuition turned out to be priceless later on.
contextSentenceKo: 호기심과 직관은 나중에 값을 매길 수 없을 만큼 소중한 것으로 밝혀졌습니다.

definition: The sum of a person's actions in this and previous states of existence, viewed as deciding their fate; destiny or fate
contextSentence: You have to trust in something. Your gut, destiny, life, karma, whatever.
contextSentenceKo: 무언가를 믿어야 합니다. 직감이든, 운명이든, 삶이든, 인연이든, 무엇이든.

definition: To become evident to the mind; to begin to be perceived or understood
contextSentence: But something slowly began to dawn on me.
contextSentenceKo: 하지만 무언가가 서서히 제게 깨달아지기 시작했습니다.

definition: To accept something less than ideal or desired; to compromise
contextSentence: If you haven't found it yet, keep looking and don't settle.
contextSentenceKo: 아직 찾지 못했다면 계속 찾으세요. 안주하지 마세요.

definition: To unexpectedly experience or be faced with something
contextSentence: Remembering that I'll be dead soon is the most important tool I've ever encountered.
contextSentenceKo: 곧 죽게 된다는 사실을 기억하는 것이 제가 접한 것 중 가장 중요한 도구입니다.

definition: A feeling of self-consciousness, shame, or awkwardness
contextSentence: All fear of embarrassment or failure, these things just fall away in the face of death.
contextSentenceKo: 창피함이나 실패에 대한 모든 두려움, 이런 것들은 죽음 앞에서 그저 사라져 버립니다.

definition: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent
contextSentence: Death is the destination we all share.
contextSentenceKo: 죽음은 우리 모두가 공유하는 목적지입니다.
